headline: GENERATION MINING CLOSES $1.3B MARATHON PACKAGE — Glencore Offtake Locked, Canada Growth Fund Takes 19.9% Stake
snippet: Generation Mining Ltd. (TSX: GENM) closed the C$240-million equity tranche of its $1.3-billion total financing package for the Marathon copper-palladium project in Northwestern Ontario on September 21, with anchor investor Canada Growth Fund contributing C$140 million for a 19.9% stake and the Canada Infrastructure Bank adding C$50 million. Glencore will purchase 100% of the polymetallic copper concentrate containing copper, palladium, platinum, gold and silver from Marathon under a cornerstone offtake arrangement that validates the project economics, with early works construction targeted to begin in Q4 2026 — making Marathon Canada's next major critical minerals mine.

headline: RARE EARTHS HOLD TRUMP BACK — China's 90% Processing Grip Softens U.S. Posture Before Thursday's Xi Summit
snippet: Multiple geopolitical analysts noted Tuesday that President Trump has adopted a markedly less combative posture ahead of the September 24 Washington summit with President Xi Jinping — the clearest signal yet that China's rare earth export controls are generating genuine policy constraints rather than just market anxiety. China controls roughly 70% of global rare-earth mining, 85% of refining capacity, and ~90% of rare-earth alloy and magnet production; US manufacturers of EVs, semiconductors, and defense systems have cited growing supply difficulty. For investors in rare earth and critical mineral explorers, the summit result — particularly any deal around export resumption or supply guarantees — is the single most important near-term sector catalyst, with a tariff suspension deadline of November 10 also on the table.

headline: DoW-BACKED U.S. TUNGSTEN PLAY: Blue Moon Drills 7.01m at 1.28% WO3 — 67,000m BLM-Approved Program Ready to Launch
snippet: Blue Moon Metals Inc. (TSXV: BMM) released assay results from its Springer Tungsten Project in Pershing County, Nevada, confirming 7.01 metres at 1.28% WO₃ and 24.25 metres at 0.22% WO₃ (including 9.55m at 0.53% WO₃) in re-assayed historical core, while simultaneously receiving BLM approval for 13 drill pads on public lands within a 67,000-metre program. The announcement arrives as The Elmet Group — the recipient of a US$450-million Department of War preferred-equity investment on September 14 to rebuild America's tungsten supply chain — has agreed to co-develop Springer alongside EQ Resources in a US$150–$175-million strategic transaction, making Blue Moon one of the most strategically underpinned junior critical-mineral plays in North America.

headline: COEUR MINING SETS $158M EXPLORATION RECORD — K-Zone at New Afton Now 1,100m+ Strike; 43.6 g/t Gold at Rainy River
snippet: Coeur Mining Inc. (NYSE: CDE) updated investors on exploration at its recently acquired New Afton (BC) and Rainy River (Ontario) mines, reporting that the K-Zone deposit at New Afton has grown to more than 1,100 metres along strike and 1,100 metres vertically following 109 km of drilling since its 2023 discovery — with a maiden M&I resource of 48 million tonnes confirmed in March 2026. Rainy River posted a highlight of 5.8 metres true-width at 43.6 g/t gold and 13 g/t silver. Total 2026 exploration spending is on pace for a company record US$158 million, more than double 2025 levels, highlighting the resource-growth leverage that distinguishes Coeur's post-New Gold acquisition portfolio.

headline: PROVINCE-SCALE PORPHYRY CONFIRMED IN AUSTRALIA — Kincora Copper Drills 312.8m Basement in Macquarie Arc with AngloGold JV
snippet: Kincora Copper Ltd. (ASX: KCC) reported that 2026 drilling at its Nevertire South and Nyngan licences in the Macquarie Arc of New South Wales has confirmed basement rock continuity across more than 40 kilometres of strike — a greater-than-5x increase relative to prior drill extent — with hole NEDD011 returning a 312.8-metre basement intersection and intensifying porphyry indicators pointing toward an undiscovered intrusive core, and hole NEDD018 hitting 1,285 ppm copper from depth. Both licences are held under earn-in JV agreements with AngloGold Ashanti Australia, meaning exploration is substantially carried while a major validates the targeting concept in one of Australia's most prolific porphyry belts.

headline: ANTIMONY HIT IN NEW BRUNSWICK BATHURST CAMP — SLAM Reports >1% Sb in 3 Samples Plus 1.97 g/t Gold, 73.5 g/t Silver
snippet: SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSXV: SXL) reported antimony assays exceeding the 1% detection limit in three samples from trenches at the Skull epithermal zone of its Moose Lake project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp, alongside gold and silver values up to 1.965 g/t Au and 73.50 g/t Ag. The stibnite (antimony) breccia zone has been traced over 242 metres of strike across eight trenches on road-accessible ground acquired in March 2026. With antimony a US-designated critical mineral and China controlling over 80% of global supply, a primary antimony discovery in a permitted Canadian mining district with co-incident gold-silver mineralization is one of the more strategically timely early-stage announcements of 2026.

headline: 473 g/t SILVER AT SILVER CLIFF — Viscount Drills 7.9m at 473 g/t Ag, 1KM OUTSIDE Current Kate Resource in Colorado
snippet: Viscount Mining Corp. (TSXV: VML, OTC: VLMGF) reported that all 10 holes in its 2026 drill program at the Silver Cliff Project in Custer County, Colorado confirmed silver mineralization outside the current Kate NI 43-101 resource boundary, headlined by hole K26-08 intersecting 13.4 metres averaging 267.6 g/t Ag including 7.9 metres at 473.2 g/t Ag and 2.92 g/t Au — located approximately 1 kilometre from the resource outline. The step-out results confirm that the Tr2/Tr3 silver-host rhyolites extend beyond the current resource limits in multiple directions, setting up a materially larger resource estimate when 2026 results are incorporated.

headline: COPPER AT $6.75/LB AND CLOSING IN — Yangshan Premium $121/T, China Grid Spend +13%; Record of $6.89/lb in Sight
snippet: COMEX copper settled at US$6.75 per pound on Tuesday, closing within US$0.14 of the all-time intraday record of US$6.89/lb set on September 9, as the Yangshan import premium rose to US$121 per tonne — its highest since November 2022 — signalling that Chinese industrial buyers are actively pulling physical metal into bonded warehouses at spot. China's power grid investment spending rose 13% year-on-year in H1 2026, the fundamental driver behind the sustained copper price strength. For junior copper developers, the convergence of near-record spot prices and major institutional financing events (see Marathon closing today) represents the most constructive project-financing environment for copper since early 2022.

headline: LITHIUM EQUITIES LIFT AS EV RESTOCKING RETURNS — Albemarle, SQM, LIT ETF Climb on Chinese Battery Demand Stabilization
snippet: Lithium equities posted modest gains Tuesday as LIT, Albemarle, and SQM all climbed on reports of Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate restocking by domestic cell manufacturers, providing a demand-side counterweight to the supply disruptions dominating headlines this week — including the revocation of CATL's Jianxiawo mine environmental approval and the UAE's A$333M takeout of Global Lithium Resources. The restocking signal is preliminary but consistent with seasonal patterns ahead of Q4 EV production ramp-ups by major Chinese automakers; sustained restocking would represent the first demand-driven price recovery catalyst after 18 months of lithium carbonate price pressure.

headline: COT GOLD SEPT 18: SPECULATORS STILL POSITIONED FOR UPSIDE — Net Longs Steady Despite Fed Hawkishness, Silver Nets Surge
snippet: The September 18 Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC — covering positions as of September 15 — showed that large speculative net-long positions in gold futures remained elevated despite Fed officials Musalem and Goolsbee signalling further rate hikes may be warranted, while silver speculative nets showed a pronounced surge in bullish positioning. The combination of persistent speculative length in gold (historically a sentiment indicator for retail mining equity interest) and growing silver longs suggests funds are not treating the hawkish Fed commentary as a signal to exit the precious metals trade — maintaining the macro backdrop that has supported junior gold and silver exploration equities through September.
